newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise in thin trading, Elbit soars.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise in thin trading, Elbit soars.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in thin and mixed trading on Sunday and traders and analysts said the market was recovering.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.52 points, or 0.84 percent, to 182.71 on an all-share turnover of only 56 million shekels against 75 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 index rose 0.49 percent to 193.25.

"During the last few days the market has been rising and starting to recover. This is a direct outcome of the big off-the-floor transactions we saw last week. Now it is clear that prices are very cheap," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets.
"It is difficult to predict how the market will behave in the future but it is clear it is starting to wake up," he said.

Elbit surged 6.75 percent to 14,228 after it said that it started negotiations for the sale of 80 percent of its Boston-based subsidiary Inframetrics Inc to a U.S. consortium for $30 million. Traders said the deal shows that Elbit is undervalued.
Elbit's parent company, Elron Electronic Industries, rose 4.0 percent to 12,135.
Bezeq Israel Telecom rose 1.5 percent to 760 after it reported second-quarter net profit rose to 155.2 million shekels from 123 million shekels in the same quarter in 1995.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu favours selling shares in Bezeq through an international public offering rather than to a strategic investor, Treasury sources said.
Tadiran jumped 4.5 percent to 1,294 following the rise of its shares on Nasdaq.
First International Bank of Israel fell 3.5 percent to 34,599 for no evident reason.
"Activity was mixed but the positive trend continues. Volume is still very low and the market was very quiet," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

The most active shares were Africa Israel Investments, which closed unchanged at 470,651 on volume of 6.9 million shekels; Koor Industries, which fell 2.0 percent to 26,681 on turnover of 2.7 million shekels; and Discount Investments, which rose 1.25 percent to 19.081 on volume of 2.5 million shekels.
